headline:
That list on
your fridge?
Let’s handle it.
intro: The loose handle, the shelf still in its box, the door that never quite closes. A practical plan for the jobs that add up.
serviceTitle: Make a little room on your to-do list.
serviceIntro: Group the small jobs into a visit that makes sense. Materials, access, and specialist requirements are reviewed first.

offers.title: Fix the everyday
offers.text: Tackle the small issues that make a home feel unfinished.

offers.title: Put it together
offers.text: Turn boxes and instructions into something useful.

offers.title: Make it feel finished
offers.text: A thoughtful hand with the final details.

story.eyebrow: MEASURE FIRST. THEN MAKE IT RIGHT.
story.title: A good visit starts with a good list.
story.text: Photos, dimensions, product instructions, and the condition of the surface make a request easier to understand. Agree the work before the tools come out.
points: Refer licensed work to the right trade

guide.title: Less guesswork. More done.
guide.intro: A small job still deserves a clear brief and realistic expectations.

notes.title: Make the list
notes.text: Describe each task and the result you want. Note dimensions, item models, wall materials, and anything that has been tried already.

notes.title: Sort the materials
notes.text: Agree who supplies fixtures, fixings, and replacement parts. A visit can stall when the right part or installation instructions are missing.

notes.title: Know the boundaries
notes.text: Electrical, plumbing, structural, and other regulated work may need a licensed specialist. This example does not claim those credentials.

notes.title: Walk through the result
notes.text: Review completed tasks and outstanding items together. Any newly discovered damage or extra work should be discussed before it is added.

faq.a: Yes. The planner creates a short project list. A real provider would review the tasks and agree a practical visit scope.
That should be agreed in advance. You can indicate whether items are already on hand or need to be sourced.

faq.q: Can every repair be handled in one visit?
faq.a: No. Hidden conditions, missing parts, or specialist requirements may change the plan. A useful website sets that expectation clearly.
